newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Jordan gets $25.6 mln in Arab central banks meet.
newsitem.headline: Jordan gets $25.6 mln in Arab central banks meet.

text.p: Arab Trade and Finance Programme on Thursday agreed to open a three credit lines worth $25.6 million to finance Jordan's food imports from Arab countries, a spokesman said.
The decision was taken on the sidelines of a meeting of central bank governors and heads of Arab League monetary agencies in the Moroccan capital of Rabat.
The United Arab Emirates-based Programme signed an agreement with Jordan's central bank governor for a $25.6 million loan over 18 months, the spokesman said.
"The loan will be devoted for Jordan's food imports from Arab League members," he said. With a $500 million capital, the fund has recently granted Jordan $46.6 million, officials said.
No other details of the latest accord were given.
A group of 18 governors of Arab central banks held their first meeting to "discuss the monetary policies of Arab countries and ways to restructure their economies," the spokesman added.

At the opening ceremony of the 20th annual session of the Council of Governors of Central Banks and Arab League Monetary Agencies, Moroccan Finance Minister Mohamed Kabbaj called on Arab states to unify their ranks and "reinforce coordination on monetary and finance policy to respond to the increasing competitiveness of regional groupings".
In their two sessions behind closed doors, the governors will examine "reports on inflation and control exchange rates, in the light of Lebanon's experience," the spokesman said.
They will determine "the common position to be taken later during the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank," he added.
Tunisia, Somalia and Djibouti were invited but did not attend the meeting, officials said, but declined other comment.
